question: Involuntary actions like breathing, salivation and peristalsis are controlled by ______.
solution:
The correct answer is __**medulla oblongata**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Involuntary actions like breathing, salivation, and peristalsis are controlled by the **medulla oblongata**.
 
• The medulla oblongata is located in the brainstem, anterior to the cerebellum.
 
• It plays a critical role in transmitting signals between the spinal cord and higher parts of the brain, and in controlling autonomic functions.
 
• It regulates essential functions such as heart rate, blood pressure, and respiratory rhythm.
 
• Damage to the medulla oblongata can result in loss of vital autonomic functions and can be life-threatening.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **hypothalamus** is involved in hormone regulation and maintaining homeostasis but does not directly control involuntary actions like breathing.
 
• The **cerebrum** is responsible for higher brain functions such as thought and action.
 
• The **cerebellum** coordinates voluntary movements like posture, balance, and coordination.
 
• The medulla oblongata is part of the brainstem, which also includes the midbrain and pons, all of which are involved in autonomic and reflex activities.
 
• The brainstem is crucial for the survival of an organism due to its control over essential bodily functions.
